findings.rule: Incident date must fall within the period of cover, the tier must cover own damage, and the peril must be a covered event (collision with an animal).
findings.explanation: The incident date of 2026-08-29 falls between inception 2025-11-01 and expiry 2026-10-31. The COMP tier covers own damage. A collision with an animal (kangaroo) is a covered event under 2.1. Premium was paid, so there was no lapse under 7.2(d). The supplied clauses contain no waiting period and no territory rule that I needed to apply. The incident was in Australia.

findings.rule: A claim must be notified within 30 calendar days of the incident date (cl. 2.1); beyond 90 days it must be declined absent a recorded 2.3 exception (cl. 2.2, 7.2(b)).
findings.calculation: days_incident_to_fnol = 2, which is within the 30 calendar day window (2 <= 30).
findings.explanation: The claim was notified 2 days after the incident, within the 30-day window. No late notification exception was needed or applied.

findings.rule: Check whether any supplied exclusion applies. Only the commercial/hire use exclusion (3.7, absolute) and the unattended vehicle with keys exclusion (3.13, theft only) are supplied; neither is triggered by the facts. No alcohol, drug, licence, unlisted driver or registration exclusion clauses were supplied, but the claim facts show no trigger for them.
findings.explanation: Vehicle use at incident matches declared private use, so clause 3.7 is not triggered. The peril is collision, so the theft-only clause 3.13 does not apply, and so clause 6.1 is not engaged. No override or exception was recorded. The driver is the policyholder with a valid licence, and registration is current. No BAC reading was recorded and no drug test was done, so there is no evidence of an alcohol or drug exclusion trigger. The fraud indicators and handler notes are outside this area.

findings.rule: Tracks are tested in order and the first met is assigned. A fraud score of 60 or more under POL-FRD-004 3.2 places the claim on the SIU track (order 1) and requires mandatory SIU referral with standard handling paused.
findings.calculation: Recorded fraud score 60 >= 60 threshold, so SIU (order 1) is met before Complex, Fast-track or Standard. The claim was assigned STANDARD (order 4) and siu_referred is false.
findings.explanation: The recorded fraud score of 60 falls in the High band, which requires mandatory SIU referral. Under the precedence rules the claim should have been triaged to SIU and standard handling paused. It was placed on the Standard track and never referred, so the track assignment is wrong and the decision to accept and pay cannot stand.

findings.rule: Every lodged claim must be triaged within 1 business day of lodgement.
findings.explanation: Triage timing was met, although the track assigned was incorrect.

findings.rule: Whether the supplied fraud indicators or the claim history (three previous claims in 22 months) trigger a mandatory referral under POL-FRD-004 5.1(f), which concerns the third claim on the same policy within 12 months. The supplied clauses do not define how the indicator codes map to scores or how prior claims under a prior policy are counted.

evidence.value: Sum insured increased from AUD 18,000 to AUD 26,000 on 20 August 2026. Claimant has lodged three previous claims in 22 months (two with Meridian under a prior policy). Claimant pressed for payment within 48 hours at first contact and quoted policy clause numbers.

findings.explanation: The claim is already SIU-eligible on score. Whether clause 5.1(f) also applies cannot be determined from the supplied clauses, since the claims were on a prior policy and the 12-month count is not given. This is noted for completeness only.

findings.rule: An assessment is required for all claims except fast-track claims where photos suffice; a desktop assessment is acceptable below the AUD 100,000 independent threshold; the assessment must be no older than 90 days at decision; a second assessment is required only if disputed, variance exceeds the greater of 30% or AUD 20,000, or a conflict of interest is recorded.
findings.calculation: Variance = 14500 - 13800 = 700; 700 / 14500 = 4.8%, below the 30% threshold (the greater of 30% or AUD 20,000 applies). Assessment age at decision is 5 days, within the 90-day limit. Claimed value of 14,500 is below AUD 100,000.
findings.explanation: An assessment was done on a standard-track claim. The desktop type is acceptable because the value is well under AUD 100,000, and no field assessment was shown to be required, so the 4.2 allocation timeframes are not triggered. The assessment was fresh at decision, and no second-assessment trigger (written dispute, variance above threshold, or conflict of interest) appears in the facts.

findings.rule: Total incurred cost must be within the approver's settlement authority (L2 = AUD 50,000). Dual approval or denial limits only apply where other rules are triggered.
findings.calculation: Total incurred 13,000 <= L2 settlement authority 50,000. Single payment of 13,000, so no splitting. Decision is an acceptance, so denial limits do not apply.
findings.explanation: The L2 approver had settlement authority above the total incurred of AUD 13,000. There was one payment, so no splitting breach. No exception, ex-gratia payment, litigation or catastrophe surge applies. The supplied clauses do not require a second approver for this claim.

findings.rule: A recorded fraud score of 60-79 (High band) requires mandatory SIU referral, and settlement is blocked pending SIU clearance. Referral is due within 1 business day of the trigger.
findings.explanation: The recorded score of 60 falls in the High band (60-79). No SIU referral was made (siu_referred is false) and there is no SIU outcome, yet the claim was accepted and 13,000 was paid. The mandatory referral was skipped and the settlement block was bypassed.

findings.rule: The fraud score must equal the sum of the catalogue points for the indicators that apply. The point values for T-02, C-05, C-04 and T-05 are not in the supplied clauses, so the score of 60 cannot be verified.
findings.calculation: H-01 = 20 points (clause 2.2). T-02, C-05, C-04 and T-05 have no supplied values, so the total cannot be calculated.
findings.explanation: Only the claimant history table (2.2) was supplied. The tables that give points for T-02, C-05, C-04 and T-05 are missing. Clause 7.1 does not affect the listed indicators, because only T-02 is listed and not T-01. The score accuracy needs review against the full catalogue. The band, and so the required action, depends on it. A score of 60 or more still requires SIU referral.

findings.rule: Decision-stage and settlement-stage documents required for this claim must be on file before an accept decision. Required here: CLAIM_FORM, ID_VERIFIED, DRIVER_LICENCE, PHOTOS, LICENCE_VERIFIED (claimed amount over 10,000), REPAIR_QUOTE_ACCREDITED, ASSESSMENT_REPORT, VEHICLE_HISTORY_CHECK (over 10,000) and BANK_VERIFIED.
findings.explanation: Every document required by the supplied clauses is on file, and the documents were complete on 2026-09-04, before the decision on 2026-09-09. STAT_DEC, PPSR_SEARCH, INDEPENDENT_ASSESSMENT, TP_DETAILS, CTP_REFERENCE and GST_DECLARATION do not apply, because the claim is under AUD 50,000, is not a total loss, has no third party or injury, and the claimant is not GST registered.

findings.rule: Appendix A requires POLICE_EVENT for 'collisions under 4.1', but clause 4.1 of POL-DOC-005 (the rule defining which collisions need a police event number) was not supplied.
findings.explanation: No police event number or POLICE_EVENT document is on file for this collision with a kangaroo. The supplied clauses do not say whether this type of collision falls under clause 4.1, so I cannot decide whether the document was required. A reviewer with clause 4.1 needs to confirm. If it was required, the accept decision was made without a decision-stage document on file.

findings.rule: Acknowledge within 2 business days of lodgement; decide a standard claim within 20 business days of docs-complete and within 4 months of lodgement; communicate the decision within 5 business days; pay within 10 business days of acceptance; status updates at least every 20 business days (10 for vulnerable claimants).
findings.calculation: Ack 1 <= 2; decision 3 <= 20 from docs-complete; decided within 4 months; communication 0 <= 5; payment 2 <= 10; max contact gap 3 <= 20; triage 1 <= 1.
findings.explanation: All service timeframes were met, so there is no service-level breach.

findings.rule: Repair-basis settlement with correct excess: driver aged 29 with 11 years full licence, so no additional excess; repair cost 53.1% is below the 75% total loss threshold; claimant not GST registered so no ITC deduction; no recovery.
findings.calculation: Expected excess = 800 basic + 0 additional = 800. Net = 13800 - 800 - 0 = 13000, matches net_paid 13000.
findings.explanation: Excess, gross settlement, GST/ITC deduction and net payment are all correct for a repair-basis claim. The vehicle is not a total loss (53.1% is not above 75%), so no Level 3 declaration was needed. No recovery applies.
